newsitem.title: USA: US technology group applauds APEC stand on tariffs.
newsitem.headline: US technology group applauds APEC stand on tariffs.

text.p: A group of U.S. computer and telecommunications companies on Monday applauded a decision by Asia-Pacific leaders to back an agreement that would substantially reduce tariffs on information technologies.

"We are pleased that President Clinton and his fellow leaders at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation council committed to an information technology agreement by the year 2000 and agreed to push for conclusion of negotiations at the World Trade Organization meeting in Singapore early next month," Rhett Dawson, president of the Information Technology Council, said at a news conference.

The council co-chairs an Information Technology Agreement Coalition with the American Electronics Association. The coalition represents about a dozen trade associations and thousands of companies interested in a global agreement eliminating tariffs on information technologies, Dawson said.

APEC's support for an agreement that "substantially eliminates" tariffs on information technologies by 2000, increases chances that World Trade Organization members will agree to the plan at next month's meeting in Singapore, said Joe Tasker, vice president and assistant general counsel for Compaq Computer Corp.
To be sure, more work was needed to reach agreement by the time trade ministers of WTO member countries gather in Singapore, Tasker said at a news conference.
Negotiators still need to work out which products an agreement would cover and a "critical mass" of countries need to accept the idea if there is to be an agreement at the WTO gathering, Tasker said.

The ITA would eliminate tariffs on a wide variety of products, including computers, semiconductors, software and telecommunications equipment. But European Union officials have complained that the United States was seeking to exclude four important product categories -- capacitors, fiber optic cables, graphic monitors and photocopiers.

Tasker said it was important for the United States to have a global agreement on eliminating information technology tariffs because those industries represent a major part of the U.S. economy and export products.

He said it was also important for Asian countries to ensure that tariffs are eliminated on their leading export products. He also said an agreement would cut costs to their consumers on increasing important information technologies.
